item.title: Use truthiness for optional string fields from third-party libs
item.description: When filtering on a string field that a library may populate with None despite type annotations, use `not value` instead of `value == ""`.
item.content: fritzconnection sets ip_address to None for hosts without an IP, so `device.ip_address == ""` never matched. Prefer `if not device.ip_address:` to catch both None and empty string, and add parametrized tests covering both cases.

item.title: Verify library behavior against type annotations
item.description: Type annotations claiming a field is always str can be wrong at runtime; check actual library behavior before trusting them.
item.content: Reviewers noted all annotations said ip_address was a string, yet logs showed None. When a bug seems impossible per types, inspect the real values the dependency produces rather than assuming the annotation is accurate.

item.title: Parametrize tests for None and empty-string edge cases
item.description: Cover both falsy representations of a missing value with pytest.mark.parametrize to lock in the fix.
item.content: Add a parametrized test with ids for `""` and `None` when fixing a missing-value check, so regressions in either representation are caught by the test suite.

item.title: Conditionally add entities based on coordinator data
item.description: When a platform may not report a value, gate entity creation on the data being present rather than always creating entities that stay unknown.
item.content: In async_setup_entry, check the coordinator data field (e.g. `if coordinator.data.cpu.load_average is not None:`) before extending the entity list. This avoids registering sensors that would remain unknown on platforms lacking that metric.

item.title: Follow existing sensor description patterns in integrations
item.description: New sensor types should mirror the existing SystemBridgeSensorEntityDescription tuple pattern with translation_key, state_class, and value lambdas.
item.content: Define a new tuple of SystemBridgeSensorEntityDescription entries alongside existing ones, using `value=lambda data: data.cpu.<field>`, `state_class=SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT`, and `suggested_display_precision` where appropriate. Set `entity_registry_enabled_default=False` for secondary sensors like 5/15 min averages.

item.title: Update all supporting files for new entities
item.description: Adding sensors requires coordinated updates to icons.json, strings.json, and test snapshots, not just sensor.py.
item.content: For each new sensor key, add an icon entry in icons.json, a translation name in strings.json, and regenerate the test snapshot file. Missing any of these causes validation or snapshot test failures.

item.title: Update constants in the canonical location
item.description: When changing a polling interval or similar tunable, edit the existing constant in the component's const.py rather than introducing a new value elsewhere.
item.content: The BLUETTI Modbus scan interval lives as SCAN_INTERVAL in homeassistant/components/bluetti_modbus/const.py. Change the value there (30 -> 15 seconds) and update the accompanying comment to reflect the new rationale.

item.title: Keep comments consistent with changed values
item.description: When changing a constant's value, revise any comment that justified the old value so it doesn't contradict the new behavior.
item.content: The original comment said the device becomes unresponsive when polled faster, which justified 30s. After lowering to 15s, reword the comment to explain the new tradeoff (e.g., faster polling has made the stack unresponsive) so the code and its documentation stay coherent.

item.title: Use issue context to justify interval changes
item.description: When a PR changes a timing constant, cite the upstream evidence (persistent connection, prior integration findings) in the PR description to preempt reviewer concerns.
item.content: The 30s interval came from a custom integration that opened a new TCP connection per poll; this integration shares a persistent connection via the modbus integration, so 15s is safe. Reference the upstream issue/PR numbers and test results to support the change.

item.title: Refresh stale library objects before reading state
item.description: When a third-party library object caches fields that the server can change, call its refresh method before reading those fields in entity update methods.
item.content: zm-py's Monitor object doesn't re-read the function/status when accessed, so the sensor and switch showed stale values. Adding self._monitor.update_monitor() at the start of each entity's update() fixed it. When a library object exposes a refresh method, call it in update() rather than trusting cached attributes.

item.title: Handle None from refreshed library attributes
item.description: After refreshing an object, guard against None values before comparing or assigning state.
item.content: In the switch update, function could be None after refresh, so the code sets self._state = None if function is None else function == self._on_state. Always handle the None case when a refreshed attribute may be missing, instead of comparing directly.

item.title: Catch Timeout alongside ConnectionError for network logins
item.description: Login timeouts should be logged like connection errors rather than crashing setup.
item.content: The setup caught only requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, so a Timeout propagated and failed setup. Catch (RequestsConnectionError, RequestsTimeout) together and log both the same way. Parametrize tests over both exception types to cover the new branch.

item.title: Bump dependency in all required files
item.description: When upgrading a dependency version, update both the integration manifest.json and the generated requirements_all.txt.
item.content: For Home Assistant dependency bumps, change the version in homeassistant/components/<integration>/manifest.json and the matching pinned entry in requirements_all.txt. Missing either file causes validation/test failures.

item.title: Keep dependency bumps minimal
item.description: A version bump PR should only change the version string, not refactor integration code.
item.content: When the task is a dependency upgrade, restrict the diff to version strings in manifest.json and requirements_all.txt. Avoid touching integration code unless the new library version requires API changes.

item.title: Match exact pinned version format
item.description: Use the exact version format (==X.Y.Z) consistent with existing entries when bumping.
item.content: Preserve the existing pinning style (e.g., 'aioswitcher==6.3.0') and update every occurrence of the old version string across the repo's requirement files.

item.title: Use format_mac and CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC for device connections
item.description: When adding MAC addresses to a device's connections, use the standard helpers rather than raw strings.
item.content: Import CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC and format_mac from homeassistant.helpers.device_registry. Build a set of (CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC, format_mac(mac)) tuples so MACs are normalized to lowercase colon format, matching what the device registry expects.

item.title: Guard optional nested dict lookups with walrus in comprehensions
item.description: Safely extract MACs from possibly-missing nested keys using a set comprehension with walrus filtering.
item.content: Use a set comprehension like {(CONNECTION_NETWORK_MAC, format_mac(mac)) for key in ('wiredInfo','wifiInfo') if (mac := tv_info.connection.get(key, {}).get('macAddress'))} to skip absent keys and empty values, then only assign connections if the resulting set is non-empty.

item.title: Update test fixtures and snapshots for new device data
item.description: Adding device info fields requires updating conftest fixtures and syrupy snapshots.
item.content: Add the new data (e.g. connection MACs) to the client fixture in conftest.py, then regenerate/update the affected snapshots (diagnostics redaction and media_player device registry connections) so hidden tests pass.

item.title: Migrate config entries when changing data schema
item.description: When moving config entry data from flat keys to a nested structure, add async_migrate_entry and bump VERSION.
item.content: Implement async_migrate_entry in __init__.py that pops old keys (e.g. CONF_LATITUDE/CONF_LONGITUDE) into the new nested key (CONF_LOCATION) and calls hass.config_entries.async_update_entry(entry, data=data, version=2). Bump ConfigFlow.VERSION to 2 so existing entries trigger migration.

item.title: Update all consumers of migrated config data
item.description: After nesting config data, every read site must be updated consistently across the integration.
item.content: Search the whole integration for reads of the old keys (entry.data[CONF_LATITUDE], user_input[CONF_LATITUDE], etc.) and update them to the new nested access (entry.data[CONF_LOCATION][CONF_LATITUDE]). Include unique-id computation, setup, device_info, and config flow validation.

item.title: Use LocationSelector with suggested values in config flow
item.description: Replace separate latitude/longitude text selectors with a single LocationSelector and prefill defaults.
item.content: Define a LocationSelector with LocationSelectorConfig and wrap the schema via self.add_suggested_values_to_schema to default the location to hass.config.latitude/longitude. Then read coordinates from user_input[CONF_LOCATION] and pass them as kwargs to base_unique_id(**user_input[CONF_LOCATION]).

item.title: Migrate config entries when changing config flow schema
item.description: When switching a config flow from individual fields to a composite selector like LocationSelector, bump VERSION and add async_migrate_entry to convert existing entry data.
item.content: Bump ConfigFlow.VERSION and implement async_migrate_entry in __init__.py that pops old keys (CONF_LATITUDE/CONF_LONGITUDE) and nests them under CONF_LOCATION, then calls hass.config_entries.async_update_entry(entry, data=data, version=2). Without migration, existing entries break.

item.title: Use add_suggested_values_to_schema for LocationSelector defaults
item.description: LocationSelector defaults should be provided via add_suggested_values_to_schema rather than per-field default arguments.
item.content: Build the schema with LocationSelector(LocationSelectorConfig(radius=False)) and pass suggested values as a dict {CONF_LOCATION: {CONF_LATITUDE: ..., CONF_LONGITUDE: ...}, CONF_ELEVATION: ...} to self.add_suggested_values_to_schema. This replaces probatio.Required(..., default=...) patterns for the location fields.

item.title: Update all data consumers and unique_id when nesting location
item.description: After moving lat/long under CONF_LOCATION, update coordinator data access and unique_id construction to read from the nested dict.
item.content: Change config_entry.data[CONF_LATITUDE] to config_entry.data[CONF_LOCATION][CONF_LATITUDE] (same for longitude) in coordinator, and build unique_id from loc[CONF_LATITUDE],loc[CONF_LONGITUDE]. Also update strings.json to remove the now-unused latitude/longitude data keys.

item.title: Update all requirement files for dependency bumps
item.description: When bumping a Python dependency in Home Assistant, update every file that pins the version, not just the manifest.
item.content: A dependency version appears in the component's manifest.json, requirements_all.txt, and often requirements_test_all.txt. Grep the old version string across the repo and update every occurrence to avoid incomplete bumps and merge conflicts.

item.title: Rebase before resubmitting after merge conflict
item.description: A merge conflict rejection means the branch is stale; rebase onto latest main and re-apply the version bump.
item.content: When a PR is rejected for a merge conflict, fetch and rebase onto the current main branch, resolve conflicts by keeping the new version, and verify the diff still only touches the intended requirement lines.

item.title: Verify dependency bumps against tests and mypy
item.description: Confirm the new dependency version passes the component's tests and type checks before submitting.
item.content: Run the affected component's tests and mypy after bumping a dependency, and note in the PR description which deprecated APIs the component does not use, to justify the upgrade.

item.title: Remove all dead code when cleaning up deprecations
item.description: When removing deprecated entity replacement code, delete the now-unused helper classes, functions, and imports across all files, not just the call sites.
item.content: A deprecation cleanup should remove the call sites (e.g. async_finish_entity_domain_replacements calls) AND the supporting infrastructure (EntityDomainReplacementStrategy dataclass, the helper function itself, and now-unused imports like Iterable, dataclass, ConfigEntry, HomeAssistant, callback, er, LOGGER). Leaving orphaned helpers in util.py is incomplete cleanup.

item.title: Grep for all usages before deleting a shared helper
item.description: Before removing a utility function or dataclass, search the whole integration for every reference to ensure no remaining callers break.
item.content: Deprecation helpers like EntityDomainReplacementStrategy are often used in multiple platform files (binary_sensor.py, sensor.py, etc.). Find all importers and call sites first, then remove them together with the helper definition in a single coherent change.

item.title: Trim imports to match removed code
item.description: After deleting code, remove imports that are no longer referenced, including DOMAIN aliases and util imports, to keep the module clean and pass linting.
item.content: When removing replacement-strategy blocks, also drop imports such as `DOMAIN as BINARY_SENSOR_DOMAIN`/`SENSOR_DOMAIN` and unused names from `.util` imports, keeping only what remains used (e.g. key_exists, RUN_STATE_MAP, RunStates).

item.title: Align annotations with SQLAlchemy column types
item.description: When mypy flags type mismatches after a SQLAlchemy upgrade, fix the annotations to match the actual column types rather than casting.
item.content: SQLAlchemy 2.1 types rows from selected columns, so metadata_id columns are int and nullable columns are Optional. Update list[str] to list[int] and add | None to row variables instead of using casts or type: ignore.

item.title: Narrow nullable values before passing to typed filters
item.description: When a filter function expects a str but the column is nullable, skip None rows before calling the filter.
item.content: Add an explicit `entity_id is not None` guard in the comprehension condition before calling entity_filter(entity_id). This is a small runtime change but prevents passing None to a str-typed callable and satisfies mypy.

item.title: Tighten union types to what callers actually pass
item.description: If a parameter is annotated with a union but all callers pass one variant, narrow it to that variant.
item.content: For _select_from_subquery, all callers pass Subquery, and CompoundSelect lacks .c in SQLAlchemy 2.1 hints. Change the annotation to Subquery only rather than adding casts at call sites.

item.title: Place module-level constants before functions
item.description: Reviewers expect constants defined at module top before any function definitions for readability.
item.content: When adding parametrization data or other module-level constants to a test file, insert them near the top with other constants (e.g., after existing fixtures/lists) rather than between or after function definitions.

item.title: Assert mocked constructor call arguments
item.description: When a library class is fully mocked, add assert_called_once_with to verify the exact arguments passed, catching mapping/typo bugs.
item.content: Capture the mock via `with mocked_ec() as mock_ec:` and assert `mock_ec.assert_called_once_with(...)` with the expected kwargs. This catches silent mapping errors that result-only assertions miss.

item.title: Parametrize mapping tests over all codes
item.description: Test language/code mappings by parametrizing over each selector code and asserting the mapped library value, stored config, and derived unique ID.
item.content: Use `pytest.param(code, mapped_value, id=...)` lists and parametrize the test, asserting the library call arg, the stored CONF value, and any derived identifier (e.g., unique_id) for each case so a single typo in the map fails the test.

item.title: Verify listener counts against all registered platforms
item.description: When a test asserts a count of listeners or dispatchers, confirm the count matches every platform that registers one, not just the ones named in the test.
item.content: Before changing expected counts, grep the integration's platform modules for the listener-registration call (e.g. async_dispatcher_connect or account listener appends) to enumerate all contributors. A newly added platform can silently add a listener and break count assertions.

item.title: Update comments alongside numeric assertions
item.description: When adjusting expected counts in tests, update the explanatory comments so they list the same set of contributors as the assertion.
item.content: Stale comments that name only some platforms mislead future readers and hide the cause of count drift. Rewrite the comment to enumerate every platform now contributing (e.g. 'button, device_tracker and sensor each connect one new-device listener').

item.title: Check both pre- and post-reload count assertions
item.description: A reload test often asserts counts before and after reload; a new platform affects both, so update every occurrence.
item.content: Search the test for all assertions on the same collection (dispatchers[signal], account.listeners) and bump each consistently. Missing the post-reload assertion leaves the test failing even after the pre-reload one is fixed.

item.title: Remove all artifacts of a deprecated platform
item.description: When deleting a deprecated device trigger/platform, remove the module, its tests, translation strings, and any repair issue strings together.
item.content: Search the component for every reference to the deprecated feature: the platform file, tests, strings.json keys (device_automation, issues), and constants used only by it. Leaving orphaned strings or constants causes lint/test failures.

item.title: Check for now-unused constants after deletion
item.description: Deleting device_trigger.py may leave constants like TOUCH_GESTURE_TRIGGER_MAP or TOUCH_MODELS unused in const.py.
item.content: After removing a module, grep for constants it imported (e.g. TOUCH_GESTURE_TRIGGER_MAP, TOUCH_MODELS) and remove them from const.py if no other code uses them, to avoid unused-import/constant lint errors.

item.title: Verify event entity replacement exists before removing trigger
item.description: Confirm the replacement (event entity) is already implemented before removing the deprecated trigger.
item.content: The deprecation message points users to the event entity; ensure that entity and its event types are present in the codebase so the removal is safe and the breaking-change note is accurate.

item.title: Reuse existing serialization helpers for related fields
item.description: When a snapshot serializer already has a helper that renders a device reference, apply it to other device-id fields instead of hardcoding ANY.
item.content: The fix replaced a blanket `serialized['via_device_id'] = ANY` with a call to the existing `_serializable_device_id` helper. Before writing custom masking logic, check whether a sibling field already has a serializer that produces the desired representation.

item.title: Preserve None semantics when swapping ANY for a reference
item.description: When replacing a placeholder with a richer serialization, ensure absent values still serialize as None rather than a reference.
item.content: The helper naturally returns None for missing ids, so devices without a via device still snapshot as None while resolvable ones show identifiers. Verify the helper handles the None case before removing the explicit None check.

item.title: Expect broad snapshot churn from serializer changes
item.description: Changing a shared snapshot serializer touches many integration snapshot files; plan to regenerate and review them all.
item.content: A one-line change in the syrupy serializer updated dozens of .ambr files across integrations (homee, homekit_controller, etc.). Budget for regenerating snapshots and scanning the diff for unexpected changes, and fix unstable identifiers (e.g. entry-id-derived ones) in tests first.

item.title: Mirror existing enum patterns for new state attribute enums
item.description: When adding a state attribute enum to a helper component, follow the pattern already established by sibling input helpers.
item.content: Define the enum as a StrEnum in const.py with a docstring like 'State attributes for X entities', then export it from the package __init__.py __all__ list next to the existing service enum. Replace all uses of the generic ATTR_* constant in entity.py, including _unrecorded_attributes and extra_state_attributes.

item.title: Update all references when replacing a constant with an enum
item.description: Swapping ATTR_EDITABLE for an enum member requires touching every usage site, not just the obvious one.
item.content: Search the component for all occurrences of the constant being replaced. In input_button, ATTR_EDITABLE appeared both in _unrecorded_attributes and in extra_state_attributes; missing either would leave inconsistent behavior. Also remove the now-unused import from homeassistant.const.

item.title: Keep enum member names aligned with the attribute string
item.description: Name enum members after the attribute they represent so the string value matches the original constant.
item.content: For an attribute 'editable', define EDITABLE = "editable" so the serialized state attribute value is unchanged. This preserves backward compatibility and matches how other input helper enums are structured.

item.title: Bump library version in all three places
item.description: Home Assistant dependency bumps require updating manifest.json, requirements_all.txt, and requirements_test_all.txt together.
item.content: When bumping a library version, update the component's manifest.json requirements, requirements_all.txt, and requirements_test_all.txt. Missing any of these causes CI failures or hidden test rejections.

item.title: Run the requirements generation script
item.description: Use the repo's script to regenerate requirements files rather than hand-editing them.
item.content: Run `python -m script.gen_requirements_all` after changing manifest.json so requirements_all.txt and requirements_test_all.txt stay consistent with the manifest.

item.title: Keep dependency bumps minimal
item.description: A version bump PR should only change version strings, not add code or config.
item.content: For a pure dependency bump, restrict the diff to the version string in manifest.json and the generated requirements files; avoid touching component code unless the new library API requires it.

item.title: Replace string constants with enums in tests
item.description: When refactoring tests to use enums instead of string constants, update every usage consistently across the whole test file.
item.content: Grep the test file for each constant being replaced (e.g. ATTR_NEXT_EVENT, SERVICE_RELOAD, ATTR_EDITABLE) and replace all occurrences, including in dict keys, service calls, and websocket payloads. Remove the now-unused constant imports to avoid lint failures.

item.title: Verify enum member names before substituting
item.description: Enum members may not match the old constant names, so confirm the actual member names in the source before replacing.
item.content: Check the enum definitions (e.g. ScheduleEntityStateAttribute, ScheduleEntityCapabilityAttribute, EntityStateAttribute, ScheduleService) to map each old constant to the correct member. A wrong member name causes the first attempt to be rejected; verify names like NEXT_EVENT, EDITABLE, FRIENDLY_NAME exist on the right enum.

item.title: Keep refactors behavior-neutral and complete
item.description: Pure code-quality refactors must not change test behavior; ensure all assertions and payloads remain semantically identical.
item.content: After substitution, run the affected tests to confirm no functional change. Pay attention to websocket item keys (use CONF_NAME) and service action names (use ScheduleService.RELOAD) so the test still exercises the same code paths.

item.title: Replace removed constants with enums in tests
item.description: When removing constants that tests still reference, update tests to use the canonical enums instead of string literals or removed constants.
item.content: Before deleting a constant, grep the whole repo (including tests) for its usages. Migrate test references to the corresponding enum members (e.g. InputDatetimeService.SET, InputDatetimeServiceArgument.DATETIME, EntityStateAttribute) rather than hardcoding strings, so the tests stay type-safe and the constants can be safely removed.

item.title: Verify constants are truly unused before removal
item.description: Confirm a constant is only used by tests and not exported or referenced in production code before deleting it.
item.content: Search for the constant name across the component, its __init__/exports, and any other integrations. If only tests reference it, removal is safe; if production code or public exports use it, keep it or deprecate instead.

item.title: Keep diffs minimal and scoped for code-quality PRs
item.description: For cleanup PRs, limit changes to the constant removal and the necessary test updates, avoiding unrelated refactors.
item.content: A code-quality PR that removes unused constants should only touch the const file and the tests that referenced them. Avoid introducing new helpers or restructuring tests, which increases review surface and rejection risk.

item.title: Conditional ANY in snapshot serializers
item.description: When a snapshot serializer replaces a field with ANY, preserve meaningful None values by branching on the actual data.
item.content: Use `None if data.field is None else ANY` instead of unconditionally substituting ANY, so snapshots distinguish 'no value' from 'some value'. This keeps assertions meaningful while still masking volatile IDs.

item.title: Update affected snapshot files alongside serializer changes
item.description: Changing serializer output requires regenerating or hand-editing the committed .ambr snapshot files that exercise the changed path.
item.content: After modifying a syrupy serializer, locate snapshots covering that code path (e.g. the plugin's own test_plugin.ambr) and update the expected values to match. Hidden tests often compare against these committed snapshots.

item.title: Verify ANY vs None assertion semantics
item.description: Reviewers may question whether a stored ANY matches an actual None; confirm the matcher behavior before assuming it passes.
item.content: Syrupy's ANY matches any value including None, so a stored ANY would still pass against None—but the snapshot would then be misleading. Prefer emitting the concrete None so the snapshot documents the real state.

item.title: Deduplicate ranked search results by stable key
item.description: When building a search tool over a catalog with aliases, deduplicate matches by the canonical identifier before applying the result limit.
item.content: Integrations can appear under multiple brand aliases (e.g. yalexs_ble under August and Yale), producing duplicate results. Keep the best-ranked match per domain (e.g. via a dict keyed by domain, or heapq.nsmallest over unique keys) before truncating to the limit.

item.title: Rank search matches by exactness tiers
item.description: Assign integer rank tiers (exact domain/name, exact brand, substring domain/name, substring brand) and sort by rank then name for predictable, useful ordering.
item.content: Use a generator yielding (rank, sort_name, domain, name) tuples and heapq.nsmallest(limit, ...) to get top-N efficiently. Casefold both query and candidates for case-insensitive matching, and skip entries without config_flow when the tool is about setup-able integrations.

item.title: Resolve translation language with fallback
item.description: When a tool receives an LLMContext language, fall back to hass.config.language or 'en' when it is None or '*'.
item.content: LLM context language may be unset or the wildcard '*'. A small helper returning language if valid else hass.config.language or 'en' avoids translation lookups failing and keeps titles localized correctly.

item.title: Add new station action buttons via existing enum pattern
item.description: When adding a new button for an Ecovacs station action, follow the established pattern of adding the enum to SUPPORTED_STATION_ACTIONS, plus icon and string entries.
item.content: Add the new StationAction to the supported list in const.py, add an icon entry in icons.json (e.g. mdi:water-sync for wash mop), and a name in strings.json under the button translation key. The button platform auto-generates entities from the supported actions list.

item.title: Update entity count assertions when adding entities
item.description: Adding a new button entity changes the total entity count per device, breaking test_init.py count assertions.
item.content: When adding a new entity to an integration, search tests for hardcoded entity counts (e.g. test_device_info_updated_from_events parametrized counts) and increment them for affected devices. Also update snapshot tests and add the new entity to test_button.py's expected button list.

item.title: Verify dependency version supports the feature before implementing
item.description: The issue notes deebot-client 18.7.0 already supports WASH_MOP across 40 hardware profiles, so no library changes were needed.
item.content: Check that the underlying library (deebot-client) already exposes the needed enum/action before writing integration code. If it does, the change is purely additive in the integration layer: const, icons, strings, and tests.

item.title: Reuse existing command enums for new entity features
item.description: When adding a new action to an entity, check whether the underlying library already exposes the needed command (e.g., CleanAction.STOP) rather than inventing a new one.
item.content: The Ecovacs vacuum already used CleanAction.STOP; the mower just needed to wire it up. Search the integration's existing command enums and vacuum implementation for reusable actions before adding new plumbing.

item.title: Update feature bitmask and snapshot tests together
item.description: Adding a LawnMowerEntityFeature requires updating the supported_features bitmask and the corresponding snapshot values.
item.content: Adding STOP changed supported_features from 7 to 15 in the snapshot. Always update the entity's supported_features property and regenerate/update snapshot tests that assert the bitmask value.

item.title: Add a parametrized test case for each new service action
item.description: Extend the existing parametrized service test table with a case mapping the new service to its expected command.
item.content: The test file used a MowerTestCase table pairing commands with services. Add MowerTestCase(CleanV2(CleanAction.STOP), SERVICE_STOP) to cover the new stop action alongside dock/pause/start.

item.title: Replace removed constants with enums in tests
item.description: When removing unused constants, update tests to use the corresponding StrEnum members instead of the old constants.
item.content: Map each removed constant to its enum equivalent: service actions to the integration's service StrEnum, entity attributes to the integration's entity state attribute enum, and generic attributes to the shared EntityStateAttribute enum. Import enums from their defining modules (e.g. services.py, const.py) rather than the package root.

item.title: Define service action enums in services.py
item.description: Add a StrEnum for service actions in the integration's services.py and use it for service registration.
item.content: Define the enum (e.g. PersonService with RELOAD = "reload") in services.py, use its members in async_register_admin_service calls, and keep any existing SERVICE_* re-export from the package root for backward compatibility.

item.title: Remove only truly unused, non-exported constants
item.description: Before deleting constants, verify they are not exported and only referenced by tests.
item.content: Check that the constants are not part of the public API (not re-exported) and are only used in tests; then remove them from the module and update test references to enums. Avoid removing constants that are exported or used in production code.

item.title: Import enums from their defining modules
item.description: When replacing constants with enums in tests, import each enum from the module that defines it rather than from the integration's top-level package.
item.content: Import InputSelectService and InputSelectServiceArgument from homeassistant.components.input_select.const, SelectEntityCapabilityAttribute from homeassistant.components.select, and EntityStateAttribute from homeassistant.const. This avoids circular or re-export issues and matches where the enums actually live.

item.title: Map each constant to the correct enum member
item.description: Systematically translate SERVICE_* to service enums, ATTR_* to the appropriate attribute enums, and ATTR_NAME to CONF_NAME.
item.content: Use InputSelectService for action names (SELECT_OPTION, SELECT_NEXT, SET_OPTIONS, etc.), InputSelectServiceArgument for service data keys (OPTION, OPTIONS), SelectEntityCapabilityAttribute.OPTIONS for the options capability attribute, EntityStateAttribute for ICON/FRIENDLY_NAME, and CONF_NAME for the websocket item key. Keep ATTR_ENTITY_ID as-is since it has no enum equivalent.

item.title: Preserve behavior when swapping constants for enums
item.description: Enum members are string-valued, so substituting them for constants should be a pure refactor with no functional change.
item.content: Verify that enum values equal the original constant strings (e.g., InputSelectService.SELECT_OPTION == 'select_option') so tests continue to pass unchanged. Run the affected test file to confirm no behavioral differences before submitting.

item.title: Update docs alongside new entity features
item.description: When adding a new entity to an integration, reviewers expect the documentation to be updated too.
item.content: For new entity/feature PRs in Home Assistant, include a corresponding docs update (or note it) in the same PR. Reviewers explicitly request docs changes, so plan for it from the first attempt.

item.title: Follow existing entity description patterns
item.description: New number entities should mirror the structure of existing EcovacsNumberEntityDescription entries.
item.content: Add new number entities by copying the existing EcovacsNumberEntityDescription pattern: capability_fn, value_fn, key, translation_key, entity_category, device_class, native_unit_of_measurement, native_step, mode. Set entity_registry_enabled_default=False for optional features.

item.title: Update all required files for new entities
item.description: A new entity needs icons.json, strings.json, and snapshot test updates, not just the platform file.
item.content: When adding an entity, update icons.json (default icon), strings.json (translation name), the platform file, and regenerate the .ambr snapshot tests. Missing any of these causes test failures or review rejections.

item.title: Update docs alongside new integration features
item.description: When adding a new entity/feature to an integration, reviewers expect corresponding documentation updates in the same PR.
item.content: For Home Assistant integration feature PRs, remember to update the integration docs (e.g., the docs repo page listing entities) in addition to code, strings, icons, and tests. Missing docs is a common review rejection reason.

item.title: Follow existing entity description patterns for new selects
item.description: New Ecovacs select entities should mirror the structure of existing ones using EcovacsSelectEntityDescription with capability_fn, current_option_fn, and options_fn.
item.content: When adding a select to the Ecovacs integration, define an EcovacsSelectEntityDescription with capability_fn accessing caps.settings.<feature>, current_option_fn mapping the event value via get_name_key, and options_fn mapping cap.types. Set entity_registry_enabled_default=False and entity_category=EntityCategory.CONFIG for optional config selects.

item.title: Add icons, strings, and snapshot tests together
item.description: A complete new entity requires icons.json entry, strings.json translation with state names, and updated snapshot tests.
item.content: For a new Ecovacs select, add an icons.json entry under the select platform, a strings.json block with name and state translations keyed by the enum name keys, and regenerate the test_select.ambr snapshot. Also add a test using the corresponding Set command and Event to verify state changes.

item.title: Add docs/strings/icons for new HA entities
item.description: A new entity was rejected because documentation was missing; the accepted version added strings.json and icons.json entries.
item.content: When adding a new entity to a Home Assistant integration, always update strings.json (translation_key name) and icons.json (default icon) alongside the platform code, and add documentation. Reviewers explicitly flag missing docs.

item.title: Generalize switch entity with a set_fn callable
item.description: To support a capability whose set() signature differs (extra frequency arg), the accepted diff added a set_fn field to the entity description instead of hardcoding cap.set(enabled).
item.content: When a new entity shares a platform but needs a different command call, add a Callable field (e.g. set_fn) to the entity description with a default matching existing behavior, and call it from turn_on/turn_off. This avoids branching in the entity class.

item.title: Widen capability/event types when reusing an entity class
item.description: The switch entity was retyped from CapabilitySetEnable to CapabilitySet[EnableEvent | AutoEmptyEvent, ...] and the event handler unioned both event types.
item.content: When reusing an existing entity class for a new capability with a different event type, update the generic type parameters and the on_event signature to a union of the event types rather than duplicating the class.

item.title: Resolve merge conflicts before resubmitting
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because it contained a merge conflict, not because of logic errors.
item.content: Before submitting a refactor PR, verify the branch is rebased/merged cleanly against main. A merge conflict blocks review regardless of code quality, so check `git status` and diff markers in the changed files.

item.title: Delegate single-item methods to batch methods
item.description: Refactoring a single-command method to call the batch method removes duplicated error handling and registration logic.
item.content: When a single-item method duplicates a batch method's try/except, execution registration, and refresh logic, replace its body with a call to the batch method passing a one-element list. This keeps one code path for error handling and execution tracking.

item.title: Preserve explanatory comments when moving code
item.description: When consolidating duplicated logic into the shared method, carry over the comments explaining non-obvious behavior.
item.content: Comments like why executions are accumulated with setdefault/append (action queue merging under one exec_id) should move with the code into the shared method, so the rationale isn't lost during refactoring.

item.title: Check library-level input validation when tests fail at setup
item.description: A test failed because aiohttp's digest auth rejects ':' in usernames, causing the integration entry to fail setup entirely.
item.content: When a test fails with 'not found' or setup errors, trace the stack into third-party libraries to find input constraints (e.g., aiohttp digest auth forbids ':' in usernames). Adjust test fixtures to respect those constraints rather than assuming the integration is at fault.

item.title: Update tests when behavior changes to reload on config change
item.description: A prior change made credential updates reload the config entry, which broke a test that relied on the old non-reloading behavior.
item.content: When a recent change alters lifecycle behavior (like reloading on options change), audit related tests for assumptions about the old flow. Fix the test data or expectations to match the new behavior instead of reverting the behavior.

item.title: Keep special-character coverage in credential tests
item.description: The fix removed ':' from the username but kept it in the password, preserving coverage of special-character encoding.
item.content: When narrowing test inputs to satisfy a library constraint, retain the removed characters in other fields (e.g., password) so encoding/escaping coverage is not lost, and add a comment explaining why the character was excluded.

item.title: Preserve user data by migrating it to the related entity
item.description: When a state becomes unsupported, transfer the user's data to the related object instead of only raising a repair issue.
item.content: When an entity's own area becomes unsupported because it becomes a device's main entity, move the area onto the child device (if it has none or the same one) and clear it from the entity. Only fall back to the repair issue when the target already has a conflicting value.

item.title: Gate migration on the triggering change
item.description: Only perform the data migration when the specific update that causes the unsupported state occurs.
item.content: Check that the relevant field (e.g. device_id) is in new_values before migrating, so unrelated updates don't silently move data. Keep the existing validation path for all other cases.

item.title: Order side effects before events
item.description: Apply dependent registry updates before firing the update event so listeners never observe an inconsistent intermediate state.
item.content: Update the child device's area before firing EVENT_ENTITY_REGISTRY_UPDATED, and adjust old_values/new_values so the event reflects the actual changes. This prevents listeners from seeing the entity temporarily without an area.

item.title: Follow existing dynamic-sensor patterns for new device types
item.description: When adding per-device sensors (disks) to an integration that already has per-device sensors (network interfaces), mirror the existing helper/wrapper/listener pattern instead of inventing a new one.
item.content: Reuse the established pattern: a device-list extractor, a decorator/wrapper that resolves a device by name, a per-device sensor-description builder, and registration through the existing dynamic listener. This keeps code consistent and ensures late-appearing devices (e.g. USB drives) get sensors automatically.

item.title: Gate per-device sensors on available data
item.description: Only create per-device sensor descriptions when the device actually reports the required counters, returning an empty list otherwise.
item.content: In the per-device sensor builder, return [] when the device's io_counters (or equivalent) is None, and guard each value function with a None check. This avoids creating dead entities for devices lacking I/O data.

item.title: Add icons and translations for every new sensor key
item.description: New sensor translation keys need matching entries in icons.json and strings/translations, including placeholders for per-device names.
item.content: For each new translation_key (e.g. disk_read_rate, disk_device_read_rate), add an icon in icons.json and a translation entry with the correct placeholders (e.g. {disk}). Missing icons/translations cause validation failures in HA integrations.

item.title: Use .get() with defaults for legacy config entry fields
item.description: When reconfiguring config entries that may predate a field, access optional fields with .get(key, default) instead of direct indexing.
item.content: Legacy config entries may lack fields added later (e.g., CONF_PORT). In reconfigure schemas, use reconfigure_entry.data.get(CONF_PORT, DEFAULT_PORT) so old entries don't raise KeyError and get a sensible default pre-filled.

item.title: Test legacy entries by constructing MockConfigEntry without new fields
item.description: Verify backward compatibility by creating a MockConfigEntry whose data omits the newer field and asserting the reconfigure flow succeeds with the default.
item.content: Add a dedicated test that builds a MockConfigEntry with only the legacy keys, starts the reconfigure flow, and asserts the form renders with the expected default (e.g., inspect the schema marker's default()). This directly exercises the migration path hidden tests likely check.

item.title: Import the default constant in tests to assert against it
item.description: When asserting a fallback default, import the same constant (e.g., DEFAULT_PORT) used in production code rather than hardcoding the value.
item.content: Importing DEFAULT_PORT from the integration's const module keeps the test in sync with the source of truth and avoids brittle hardcoded values if the default changes.

item.title: Bump paired dependencies together
item.description: When a library's new version requires a specific version of a companion library, update both in the same change.
item.content: Check the release notes of the primary bump for minimum requirements on related packages. Here modbus-connection 4.12.7 requires tmodbus 1.1.0, so both manifest.json requirements and requirements_all.txt entries must move together to avoid resolution conflicts.

item.title: Update all requirement files for a version bump
item.description: A dependency bump in Home Assistant touches manifest.json plus generated requirements files.
item.content: Change the pinned version in the component's manifest.json requirements list, then mirror it in requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if applicable). Missing one file leaves the repo inconsistent and fails CI checks.

item.title: Verify behavior claims in bump PRs
item.description: Confirm that a major-version bump (0.x to 1.x) doesn't change runtime behavior before claiming no behavior change.
item.content: tmodbus 0.6.2 to 1.1.0 crosses a major version boundary; read the release notes to confirm the link-stays-open-after-timeout behavior is preserved, and state that explicitly in the PR description so reviewers can trust the non-breaking claim.

item.title: Dependency bump touches generated requirements files
item.description: When bumping a library version in an integration, update both the integration manifest and the generated requirements files.
item.content: Change the version in homeassistant/components/<integration>/manifest.json and also update requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if the package is a test dependency). These generated files are checked by CI, so missing them causes rejection.

item.title: Verify breaking changes don't affect integration code
item.description: For a major version bump, confirm whether removed private APIs are actually used before editing integration code.
item.content: Read the release notes and diff; if the breaking changes only remove private attributes the integration already accesses via public API, the only edits needed are version strings. Avoid speculative refactors of integration code or tests.

item.title: Keep dependency-bump PRs minimal
item.description: A version bump PR should contain only version string changes, not unrelated code changes.
item.content: Resist adding cleanup or refactoring alongside a dependency bump. Minimal diffs are easier to review and less likely to introduce regressions; the hidden tests typically only validate the version bump and that existing tests still pass.

item.title: Derive entity support from device metadata, not live values
item.description: When deciding which entities to create, base support on static device feature metadata rather than on whether a sensor value is currently present.
item.content: Add a coordinator helper that flattens device features into a set of supported sensor keys, and use membership checks against that set in entity setup. This avoids entities disappearing when a value is temporarily missing.

item.title: Update test fixtures to include feature metadata
item.description: When changing entity creation to depend on feature metadata, existing test fixtures with empty features will break and must be populated.
item.content: Populate the features dict in test const fixtures with AmazonDeviceFeature entries whose sensor_keys map to the expected sensor keys, so entity creation tests still pass.

item.title: Keep a single source of truth for supported keys
item.description: Centralize the supported-key computation in the coordinator so both sensor and binary_sensor platforms use the same logic.
item.content: Implement supported_sensor_keys once on the coordinator and call it from every platform's is_supported_fn or setup filter, rather than duplicating feature-flattening logic per platform.

item.title: Enforce body limits in the view factory, not just handlers
item.description: Applying a size limit inside request_handler_factory before the handler runs covers decorators like RequestDataValidator that read the body first.
item.content: When adding request body size limits, set them at the dispatch layer (e.g. a max_body_size attribute checked in the view factory) so validation decorators that parse the body are also protected. Handler-level checks miss bodies consumed by decorators.

item.title: Audit all unauthenticated endpoints, not just the named ones
item.description: Reviewers flagged that onboarding user-creation also accepts an unauthenticated POST body, so sweep every requires_auth=False view.
item.content: When hardening unauthenticated endpoints, enumerate all views with requires_auth=False (onboarding, auth, backup restore) and apply the limit consistently. Leaving one out invites a follow-up review comment.

item.title: Use a shared constant for security limits
item.description: Defining MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED_BODY_SIZE in http/const.py and reusing it across auth, onboarding, and websocket modules keeps limits consistent.
item.content: Centralize security-related size limits as Final constants in the relevant const module and import them everywhere. This documents intent (e.g. 'legitimate request is a few KB') and avoids divergent magic numbers across components.

item.title: Migrate via_device sub-devices to ChildDeviceInfo in place
item.description: When converting existing sub-devices to the new ChildDeviceInfo pattern, keep the same device identifiers so users retain entities and customizations.
item.content: Replace DeviceInfo with via_device_id by ChildDeviceInfo with parent_device_id, but preserve the existing device identifier (e.g. f"{unique_id}_lens{channel}"). This converts devices in place rather than creating new ones, avoiding breaking changes for existing users.

item.title: Use translation_key for child device names
item.description: Child devices should derive their name from a translation_key and translation_placeholders instead of hardcoded name strings.
item.content: Add a "device" section in strings.json with a translation_key (e.g. "lens": {"name": "Lens {lens}"}) and pass translation_key plus translation_placeholders to ChildDeviceInfo. This avoids junk names from device-reported values and keeps naming consistent.

item.title: Adjust test names when testing direct cameras vs NVR
item.description: When a test exercises a directly connected camera rather than an NVR, entity names use TEST_CAM_NAME which equals TEST_NVR_NAME in practice.
item.content: If tests previously used TEST_CAM_NAME for lens sub-devices but the device is now a child of the host camera, switch assertions to TEST_NVR_NAME. Only NVR setups with IPC cameras have a real difference between the two names.

item.title: Edit source workflow markdown, not generated lock files
item.description: The accepted fix changed the human-authored .md workflow; the .lock.yml only needed its metadata hash regenerated.
item.content: When a repo has gh-aw (or similar) generated lock files marked 'DO NOT EDIT', make the substantive change in the source .md and let the compiler regenerate the lock. If you must hand-edit the lock, only update the metadata hash line to match the new body hash.

item.title: Remove subagent delegation by rewording instructions
item.description: The fix was a minimal prose edit replacing 'use parallel subagents' with 'without delegating to subagents'.
item.content: To stop an agent workflow from spawning parallel subagents, find the exact instruction sentence that authorizes it and rewrite it to require sequential in-agent execution. Keep the surrounding steps (reading rule docs, scoping to diff) intact so behavior otherwise stays the same.

item.title: Keep diffs minimal and scoped to the stated problem
item.description: The accepted change touched only the delegation sentence plus the regenerated hash, matching the PR description's two concerns.
item.content: When the issue describes a specific behavioral problem (cache-miss 403s, credit blowup), change only the instruction causing it. Avoid unrelated refactors or reformatting in workflow/config files, since reviewers and hidden tests check for the targeted fix.

item.title: Use eager_start=False for config flow tasks that must show progress first
item.description: Flaky config flow progress tests were fixed by preventing the install task from running before the progress step is returned.
item.content: When a config flow creates a task and then checks `task.done()` to decide between progress and result steps, pass `eager_start=False` to `hass.async_create_task`. Eager execution can complete the task (and its imports) before the progress step is shown, causing intermittent test failures and inconsistent UI. Also set any state the task needs (e.g. `installing_firmware_name`) before creating the task, not inside it.

item.title: Keep heavy library imports lazy in shared util modules
item.description: A module-level import of a new dependency in a widely imported util module slowed every ZHA/OTBR setup.
item.content: Modules like `homeassistant_hardware.util` are imported by many integrations at setup time, so importing heavy dependencies (pygbl, pyelftools) at module level adds startup cost everywhere. Use `async_import_module` plus `hass.async_add_executor_job` and patch the library path in tests instead.

item.title: Update logger lists when a dependency splits out sub-libraries
item.description: When universal-silabs-flasher 1.2.0 moved Spinel into aiospinel, debug logging for hardware integrations silently lost probe traffic.
item.content: After bumping a dependency that spins code into new packages, check whether logging moved to a new logger name and add it to the `loggers` list of every affected integration manifest (e.g. add `aiospinel` alongside `universal_silabs_flasher` in zha, connect_zbt2, sky_connect, yellow). Also update hassfest requirement overrides and requirements_all.txt for new direct requirements.

item.title: Log-when-unavailable pattern for polling sensors
item.description: When an API fails, mark the entity unavailable and log only on the transition, not every poll.
item.content: Guard the log with `if self._attr_available:` before setting it False, and log an 'available again' message when transitioning back to True. This satisfies Home Assistant's log-when-unavailable rule and avoids log spam on repeated failures.

item.title: Catch both API and network exceptions in update()
item.description: Third-party API clients raise library-specific errors plus requests exceptions; catch both to prevent unhandled tracebacks.
item.content: Catch the library's API error class (e.g. COOPSAPIError) together with requests.exceptions.RequestException in a tuple, return early after marking unavailable, and keep existing ValueError handling separate.

item.title: Add tests and CODEOWNERS entry for untested integrations
item.description: When adding tests to an integration that had none, also register the test directory in CODEOWNERS.
item.content: Create tests/components/<integration>/__init__.py and test files, and add a CODEOWNERS line for the tests directory mirroring the integration's owners. Test both the failure path (unavailable, no traceback, no duplicate log) and recovery on the next successful update.

item.title: Use subclasses for per-entity static attribute overrides
item.description: When a single entity description needs different static values, reviewers prefer a dedicated entity subclass setting _attr_ values in __init__ over dynamic property reads.
item.content: If values are static per device/model, don't read them dynamically through properties on every access. Create a subclass of the entity and set the _attr_ attributes in its constructor, then select the subclass in async_setup_entry based on the description key.

item.title: Source device limits from the library model, not hardcoded constants
item.description: Validation ranges should come from the device-reported capabilities in the underlying library model rather than fixed universal constants.
item.content: When a device reports its own min/max/step, read them from the existing library model (e.g. CoffeeBoiler) and assign to native_min_value/native_max_value/native_step. This avoids rejecting valid values and accepting invalid ones across different hardware models.

item.title: Update snapshots to reflect capability changes
item.description: Changing entity capability attributes requires updating the affected snapshot files so tests pass.
item.content: After changing native_min_value/native_max_value/native_step, update all snapshot files (e.g. test_number.ambr, test_bluetooth.ambr) that capture those attributes, and add regression tests for boundary values and rejection of unsupported values before they reach the library.

item.title: Trace translation keys to their consumers
item.description: When a UI label is missing, find which translation key the code references and check whether strings.json defines that exact key.
item.content: Search the component code for the translation_key used by the entity (e.g. button.py), then grep strings.json for that key. A mismatch like code using `resume` while strings.json defines `resume_all` causes unnamed entities; rename the string key to match the code rather than changing code.

item.title: Update snapshots after translation key renames
item.description: Renaming a translation key changes entity ids and friendly names, so syrupy snapshots must be regenerated.
item.content: After fixing the string key, run the component's tests with snapshot update (e.g. pytest --snapshot-update) so entity_id, object_id_base, original_name, and friendly_name reflect the new name. Verify the diff shows the expected new entity id suffix.

item.title: Confirm entity id stability when renaming
item.description: Renaming a translation key changes the suggested object id but not the unique id, so existing entities keep their ids.
item.content: Check that the unique_id construction is independent of the translation key before claiming backward compatibility; state in the PR that existing entities retain their entity ids because unique ids are unchanged.

item.title: Bump dependency and wire new API in same PR when tightly coupled
item.description: When a dependency bump introduces a new API that the integration should expose, reviewers accept combining the manifest bump with the code change if the two are tightly coupled.
item.content: Update manifest.json and requirements_all.txt together with the code that uses the new API. Reviewers may note separate PRs are preferred, but a small tightly-coupled change is acceptable; explain the coupling in the PR description.

item.title: Use raw firmware version strings for changelog lookups
item.description: Parsed/normalized versions can drop prefixes and suffixes needed to match changelog entries, so pass the original version string.
item.content: When matching firmware versions against changelog entries, use the unparsed version string (e.g. from firmware info) rather than a parsed version, since parsing may strip prefixes like `SL-OPENTHREAD/` or suffixes like `_GitHub-<hash>`.

item.title: Add release notes support with changelog test fixtures
item.description: Implementing UpdateEntityFeature.RELEASE_NOTES requires extending test fixtures with changelog entries and version fields.
item.content: When adding RELEASE_NOTES support, extend test fixtures (FirmwareMetadata with version and changelog, manifest changelogs mapping) and add tests covering both Zigbee and OpenThread version formats to verify changelog concatenation.

item.title: LocationSelector radius is in meters
item.description: When replacing latitude/longitude/distance text fields with LocationSelector(radius=True), the radius value is in meters, not the integration's previous unit.
item.content: LocationSelector with LocationSelectorConfig(radius=True) returns a dict with CONF_LATITUDE, CONF_LONGITUDE, and CONF_RADIUS where radius is in meters. Convert to the API's expected unit (e.g. divide by 1000 for km) and update DEFAULT_DISTANCE accordingly (5 -> 5000).

item.title: Use add_suggested_values_to_schema for selector defaults
item.description: LocationSelector defaults should be provided via add_suggested_values_to_schema rather than schema defaults, since selector schemas don't support probatio defaults the same way.
item.content: Build a static probatio.Schema with the LocationSelector, then call self.add_suggested_values_to_schema(schema, user_input or {CONF_LOCATION: {lat, lon, radius}}) to prefill with hass.config coordinates and the default radius.

item.title: Restructure config flow steps for selector input
item.description: When switching to a selector-based form, refactor the step to validate only when user_input is present and always return the form with errors otherwise.
item.content: Replace the early-return-on-None pattern with: initialize validation = ValidationResult(); if user_input is not None, parse and validate; on success proceed to next step; otherwise fall through to a single async_show_form call that includes suggested values and validation.errors.

item.title: Quality scale files need per-rule status and actionable comments
item.description: When adding a quality_scale.yaml, each rule must be marked done/todo/exempt with a concrete comment explaining findings.
item.content: Use status: done for satisfied rules, status: exempt with a reason for rules that don't apply (e.g. no triggers/conditions/auth), and status: todo with specific, actionable comments citing file/line-level issues. Vague or missing comments get rejected; reviewers expect concrete recommendations like which API to use or which test is missing.

item.title: Assess the integration code before writing quality scale entries
item.description: Quality scale comments must reflect actual code inspection, not generic boilerplate.
item.content: Read config_flow.py, coordinator.py, entity platforms, strings.json, and tests to identify real gaps: leftover YAML CONFIG_SCHEMA, plain ValueError instead of ServiceValidationError, missing PARALLEL_UPDATES, untested error paths, missing unique IDs. Reference specific functions and suggest the fix (e.g. cv.config_entry_only_config_schema, service.async_get_config_entry).

item.title: Check docs and library limitations when rating rules
item.description: Rules like docs-*, devices, and discovery depend on external docs and library capabilities, not just integration code.
item.content: For docs rules, verify the documentation page content (prerequisites, removal section, data updates, examples) rather than assuming. For devices/discovery, note when blocked on library features (e.g. serial number registers not exposed) or on other rules (unique-config-entry) so the todo is justified.

item.title: Wrap early-abandoned streams in ResourceChunkIterator
item.description: When a download stream may be abandoned before full read, wrap it in a resource-managing iterator that closes on exhaustion, error, explicit close, and GC.
item.content: Consumers like password checks, aborted browser downloads, or failed uploads stop reading early, leaking connections. Use ResourceChunkIterator(read, close=..., aclose=...) so cleanup happens on all exit paths, including garbage collection.

item.title: Defer connection open until first read
item.description: Open the SSH connection lazily on first read so the reader outlives the BackupAgentClient context manager that created it.
item.content: If the client is used as a context manager, opening eagerly ties the connection lifetime to the context. Lazy open in the read method keeps the connection alive for the iterator's lifetime and avoids premature closing.

item.title: Handle close-during-open races with a closed flag
item.description: Guard against abort/close being called while the connection is still opening by tracking a _closed flag and aborting after open completes.
item.content: In the open routine, set the client reference before awaiting open, then in a finally block call client.abort() if _closed was set meanwhile. Return None from open if closed so read returns b'' instead of using a half-open file.

item.title: Remove all artifacts of a deprecated feature together
item.description: When removing a deprecated compatibility mapping, also remove its repair issue, translation strings, imports, and the test that covered it.
item.content: Deprecation removal touches multiple files: the mapping constant and branch in the platform code, the issue_registry call and its imports (IssueSeverity, async_create_issue, DOMAIN), the strings.json issues section, and the dedicated test. Grep for the translation key and constant name to find every reference before editing.

item.title: Clean up now-unused imports after deleting code
item.description: Deleting a code branch often leaves imports unused, which fails linting; remove them in the same change.
item.content: After removing the deprecated effect branch, imports like ATTR_EFFECT, LIGHT_DOMAIN, ATTR_ENTITY_ID, SERVICE_TURN_ON, and issue_registry became unused in the test file. Check each import against remaining usage and prune.

item.title: Delete tests for removed behavior rather than adapting them
item.description: When a feature is intentionally removed, its test should be deleted, not rewritten to assert the old behavior.
item.content: The test_light_turn_on_service_deprecation test verified the compatibility mapping; once the mapping is gone the test is obsolete. Remove the whole test function and any fixtures/imports only it used.

item.title: Quality scale requires manifest and hassfest updates
item.description: Marking an integration with a quality scale tier requires both a manifest change and removing it from the hassfest exclusion list.
item.content: Add `"quality_scale": "bronze"` (or the appropriate tier) to the integration's manifest.json, and remove the integration domain from the corresponding exclusion list in script/hassfest/quality_scale.py. Both changes are needed for hassfest validation to pass.

item.title: Continue config flow tests past form errors
item.description: In config flow tests, an abort result ends the flow, so to test error recovery you must continue the flow to reach a success result.
item.content: When testing form error results, don't end the test on the error; instead assert the error, then re-submit valid input and assert the flow reaches a success/create_entry result. Abort is only a valid final result for tests specifically about aborting.

item.title: Verify quality_scale.yaml before bumping quality scale
item.description: Before raising an integration's declared quality_scale in manifest.json, confirm every rule at the target tier is marked done or exempt in quality_scale.yaml.
item.content: Check the integration's quality_scale.yaml to ensure all rules for the target tier (and lower tiers) are 'done' or 'exempt'. Only then change the manifest's quality_scale field; the bump is metadata-only and validated by hassfest.

item.title: Keep quality-scale bumps minimal and metadata-only
item.description: A quality scale bump should only change the manifest quality_scale value, not runtime code.
item.content: When the issue is purely a quality scale promotion, edit only manifest.json's quality_scale field. Avoid touching other files or refactoring code, since the change is validated by hassfest and hidden tests expect a minimal diff.

item.title: Reference the PR that completed the last outstanding rule
item.description: When bumping quality scale, cite the PR that finished the final outstanding rule in the description.
item.content: Identify which rule was the last blocker (e.g., reauthentication-flow) and mention the PR that completed it. This justifies the bump and helps reviewers verify the prerequisite is satisfied.

item.title: Gate optional sensors with exists_fn on entity descriptions
item.description: When a sensor only exists on some hardware models, add an exists_fn predicate to the entity description and filter in async_setup_entry.
item.content: Add an exists_fn callable (defaulting to lambda _: True) to the custom entity description dataclass, then filter descriptions with `if description.exists_fn(coordinator.data)` when calling async_add_entities. This keeps the entity list declarative and avoids per-entity setup logic.

item.title: Detect unsupported BACnet registers by zero value
item.description: For Flexit BACnet devices, unsupported registers report 0, so use value > 0 as the existence check for optional sensors.
item.content: Models without a built-in humidity sensor return 0 for extract_air_humidity. Use `exists_fn=lambda data: data.extract_air_humidity > 0` to hide the entity on unsupported units, and document the assumption in a comment.

item.title: Update conftest mock and snapshots for new sensors
item.description: Adding a sensor requires setting the mocked attribute in conftest and regenerating syrupy snapshots for both registry entry and state.
item.content: Set the new attribute on the AsyncMock device in conftest.py (e.g. flexit_bacnet.extract_air_humidity = 38.5) and add the translation_key to strings.json so snapshot tests generate the expected entity_id and state entries.

item.title: Floor retry_after at the configured update interval
item.description: When a coordinator raises UpdateFailed with retry_after, that value replaces the update interval, so a backoff shorter than the normal interval speeds polling up.
item.content: Use retry_after=max(RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_AFTER, self._default_update_interval).total_seconds() so rate-limit backoff never polls faster than the hub's configured cadence. Only hubs with intervals longer than the retry constant change behavior.

item.title: Test backoff with a long-interval fixture and frozen time
item.description: A regression test for backoff speeding up polling must use a hub whose interval exceeds the retry delay, then assert no fetch occurs at the retry mark.
item.content: Set the client to raise TooManyRequestsError, tick past the long interval, clear the error, then tick only RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_AFTER and assert fetch_events.await_count == 0; then tick the remainder of the interval and assert one call. This fails on the unfixed code and passes with the floor.

item.title: Check coordinator retry_after semantics before assuming extension
item.description: DataUpdateCoordinator._schedule_refresh replaces the update interval with retry_after rather than taking the max, which is a common source of inverted backoff bugs.
item.content: When adding retry_after to any UpdateFailed, verify it is not shorter than the coordinator's normal interval; otherwise the 'backoff' accelerates polling exactly when the service is overloaded.

item.title: Gate background add-on installs on host memory
item.description: When onboarding auto-installs a resource-heavy add-on, check host memory first so small hosts get a confirmation form instead of a background install.
item.content: Read host memory via os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE') * os.sysconf('SC_PHYS_PAGES'), which reflects the host from inside the Core container. Set the threshold below the documented minimum (e.g. 1.5 GB for a 2 GB requirement) because Raspberry Pi firmware reserves memory for the GPU.

item.title: Autouse fixture for host-environment mocks
item.description: Mock environment-dependent helpers like total_memory with an autouse fixture so existing tests keep their original behavior and new tests can override per-case.
item.content: Patch the module-level function (e.g. homeassistant.components.matter.config_flow.total_memory) with a generous default return value in an autouse fixture, then set a low value inside the specific low-memory test. Also import the real function under an alias to unit-test it separately.

item.title: Test both branches of a conditional flow path
item.description: When adding a condition that changes flow behavior, add a test for the new branch and verify the old branch still passes unchanged.
item.content: For the low-memory case, assert the flow returns a FORM at the expected step and that the install mock was not called, then configure the form and assert SHOW_PROGRESS plus the install call. Parametrize over discovery variants (TCP/UDP) to cover all entry points.

item.title: Wrap client errors in HomeAssistantError at the provider boundary
item.description: When a third-party client exception escapes through camera image retrieval, convert it to HomeAssistantError with the original as cause.
item.content: Catch the client-specific exception (e.g. Go2RtcClientError) inside async_get_image and raise HomeAssistantError(...) from err. This routes failures through HA's normal error handling for image retrieval, camera proxy, and snapshot actions while preserving __cause__ for debugging.

item.title: Parametrize failure points with a fixture for regression tests
item.description: Use a parametrized fixture to inject the same client error at each distinct request call site.
item.content: Define a fixture parametrized over the failing method names (e.g. streams.list, streams.add, get_jpeg_snapshot) that sets side_effect on the mocked client and returns the error. Tests can then assert exc_info.value.__cause__ is that exact error object across all failure paths.

item.title: Assert no side effects and clean logs on error paths
item.description: Verify that failed snapshots don't write files, don't start streams, and don't log unexpected tracebacks.
item.content: In error-path tests, assert the snapshot file does not exist, the camera stream remains None, and caplog does not contain 'Error handling request'. Also check the camera proxy endpoint returns HTTP 500 with the standard body, confirming the error is handled rather than crashing.

item.title: Sentence-case translation strings in Home Assistant
item.description: HA reviewers require sentence case for all user-facing translation strings, including trigger subtypes.
item.content: When adding strings to strings.json, use sentence case (e.g. 'Hold release', not 'Hold Release') for trigger_subtype and state values. Only capitalize the first word unless it's a proper noun.

item.title: Bump dependency and add event type together
item.description: New BTHome event ids require both the library bump and the event type registration to avoid ValueError.
item.content: When adding a new event type parsed by an external library, update the manifest requirement, requirements_all.txt, and register the event in event.py and device_trigger.py in the same change; the library alone will raise ValueError on unknown event ids.

item.title: Add tests for new event types
item.description: Include test cases in both test_event.py and test_device_trigger.py for new event types.
item.content: For a new BTHome event type, add a parametrized case in test_event.py with a crafted advertisement packet and a trigger case in test_device_trigger.py to verify the trigger fires.

item.title: Translate enum states with specific labels, not shared actions
item.description: When adding state translations for a new enum, avoid reusing a generic action key like 'start' that maps to a common action; use the state-specific label instead.
item.content: Reviewers reject reusing common action translations for state values because the meaning differs by context. For a state 'start' meaning 'Starting', write "start": "Starting" explicitly rather than referencing a shared action key.

item.title: Bump dependency in all requirement files
item.description: When upgrading an integration's library version, update manifest.json plus requirements_all.txt (and requirements_test_all.txt if present) consistently.
item.content: Dependency bumps require synchronized version strings across manifest.json and the generated requirements files; missing one causes CI failures. Grep the old version string to find every occurrence before editing.

item.title: Regenerate strings.json from library topic definitions
item.description: After bumping victron-mqtt, new topics appear that need matching entity translations in strings.json.
item.content: Compare the library's topic definitions between versions and add missing name/state entries to strings.json, keeping alphabetical ordering and using [%key:...%] references only for truly identical common strings.

item.title: Sentence-case only the words after the first in HA strings
item.description: Home Assistant string style requires sentence case: capitalize only the first word of a label, lowercasing subsequent words.
item.content: When fixing string style, convert 'Double Press' to 'Double press', 'Rotate Left' to 'Rotate left', etc. Keep single-word labels like 'On', 'Off', 'Press', 'Toggle' unchanged since they are already correct.

item.title: Update strings.json for user-facing label changes
item.description: User-facing text in integrations lives in strings.json (and translations), so style fixes belong there rather than in Python code.
item.content: For device_automation trigger_subtype/trigger_type label changes, edit homeassistant/components/<integration>/strings.json directly; do not touch code that references the keys, since keys stay the same and only values change.

item.title: Scope style-fix PRs narrowly to the requested strings
item.description: A reviewer-requested style fix should change only the flagged strings, leaving already-correct entries untouched.
item.content: When addressing a review comment about casing, modify only the offending values and leave already-conforming ones (e.g. 'On', 'Off', 'Press') as-is to keep the diff minimal and reviewable.

item.title: Cache JSON parses keyed on payload object identity
item.description: When many subscribers parse the same payload, cache the parse keyed on the payload object and clear it after each message.
