item.content: MQTT hands every subscriber of a topic the same payload object, so a module-level cache comparing `payload is self.payload` lets all templates share one `json_loads`. Clear the cache in the client after dispatching the message so stale parses never leak across messages.

item.title: Never cache mutable payload types
item.description: Skip caching for bytearray (and similar mutable buffers) since they can change in place, invalidating the cached parse.
item.content: A bytearray payload can be mutated in place after parsing, so caching it by identity would return a stale parse. Guard the cache write with `if not isinstance(payload, bytearray)` and add a test that mutates a bytearray in place to prove the cache is bypassed.

item.title: Add optional pre-parsed argument without breaking callers
item.description: Extend a shared helper with a keyword-only sentinel-defaulted argument so existing callers keep their behavior.
item.content: Add `*, value_json: Any = _SENTINEL` to `Template.async_render_with_possible_json_value`: when the sentinel is passed, parse as before; when UNDEFINED, skip setting value_json; otherwise use the supplied value. This keeps backward compatibility while letting callers that already parsed avoid duplicate work.

item.title: Bump dependency in all three files
item.description: A Home Assistant dependency bump requires updating manifest.json, requirements_all.txt, and requirements_test_all.txt together.
item.content: When bumping a library version, update the integration's manifest.json requirements, requirements_all.txt, and requirements_test_all.txt (if the package is listed there). Missing any of these causes CI failures or hidden test failures.

item.title: Preserve the PR template when editing
item.description: Reviewers reject PRs that delete or fail to fill in the repository's pull request template.
item.content: Keep the full PR template intact and tick the relevant checkboxes (e.g., dependency upgrade, code quality). Do not strip sections; reviewers explicitly ask for the template to be restored.

item.title: Verify upstream changelog before bumping
item.description: Confirm the new library version actually contains the fixes described in the PR before changing requirements.
item.content: Check the upstream compare/changelog link to confirm the target version includes the claimed bugfixes, then bump to exactly that version across all requirement files.

item.title: Update both CODEOWNERS and manifest.json for codeowner changes
item.description: Adding a codeowner in Home Assistant requires editing two files, not just one.
item.content: When adding a codeowner for an integration, update both the root CODEOWNERS file (adding entries for the component and its tests directory) and the integration's manifest.json codeowners array. Missing either causes validation failures.

item.title: Match CODEOWNERS entry format to surrounding lines
item.description: CODEOWNERS entries must follow the existing alphabetical/formatting convention to pass checks.
item.content: Add CODEOWNERS lines in the correct alphabetical position, with separate entries for /homeassistant/components/<domain>/ and /tests/components/<domain>/, each mapping to the same owner handle.

item.title: Expect non-code review requests on trivial PRs
item.description: A rejected first attempt may be due to process (e.g., Discord contact) rather than code errors.
item.content: For small metadata PRs, review comments like 'send me a message on Discord' indicate a process requirement, not a code defect; the underlying diff may already be correct, so focus on satisfying the process ask.

item.title: Use primary_display_category for device-type filtering
item.description: When deciding which Alexa devices become a given platform entity, filter on the device's primary display category rather than inspecting feature sets.
item.content: Reviewers preferred filtering devices by `primary_display_category` (e.g. == "LIGHT") over checking individual features, since it is more robust and extensible as more devices are added. Use feature inspection only for capability details like effects.

item.title: Wrap coordinator API calls with alexa_api_call for error capture
item.description: All coordinator API invocations should go through the shared alexa_api_call context manager so errors are translated consistently.
item.content: A reviewer flagged a direct `coordinator.api.call_feature_operation` call that bypassed `alexa_api_call`. Always wrap API calls in `async with alexa_api_call(self.coordinator):` to capture and translate errors uniformly across platforms.

item.title: Guard brightness conversions against 0/1% edge cases
item.description: When mapping HA brightness (0-255) to a device scale, verify the minimum value does not collapse to 0 and cause failures.
item.content: A reviewer questioned whether brightness 1% would convert to 0 and fail. Use `brightness_to_value`/`value_to_brightness` with an explicit scale like (1, 100) and test the lowest brightness value to ensure it maps to a valid non-zero device value.

item.title: Bulk removal across many integration config flows
item.description: When removing a deprecated API call used across many integrations, sweep every integration's config_flow.py rather than only the ones named in the issue.
item.content: Grep the whole repo for the symbol (e.g. `_set_confirm_only`) to find all call sites, including ones in components not mentioned in the issue text. Remove each call and any now-unused imports or context keys in the same pass.

item.title: Keep the removed API as a reporting no-op
item.description: Instead of deleting the method outright, turn it into a no-op that reports usage so core integrations fail loudly if the call is reintroduced.
item.content: Implement the stub to raise for core integrations and only log/ignore for custom integrations, matching the issue's stated migration policy. This preserves backward compatibility for third-party code while enforcing removal in core.

item.title: Update the context type when dropping a context key
item.description: Removing a flag from flow context requires editing the TypedDict (ConfigFlowContext) as well as all writers and readers.
item.content: Search for the key name in type definitions and tests, not just call sites. Hidden tests likely assert the key is absent from the context type and that no core flow sets it.

item.title: Deprecate YAML via issue registry in async_setup
item.description: When deprecating YAML config for an integration, create a repair issue in async_setup before processing the config.
item.content: In async_setup, after checking DOMAIN in config, call async_create_issue with HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN, issue_id f"deprecated_yaml_{DOMAIN}", translation_key="deprecated_yaml", is_fixable=False, issue_domain=DOMAIN, and translation_placeholders containing domain and integration_title. Import DOMAIN as HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN from homeassistant.core and IssueSeverity/async_create_issue from helpers.issue_registry.

item.title: Test deprecation with issue_registry fixture
item.description: Verify the deprecation issue is created by setting up the component from YAML and asserting on the issue registry.
item.content: Use the issue_registry fixture, patch the integration's update method to avoid network calls, call async_setup_component with a full YAML config dict, await hass.async_block_till_done(), then assert issue_registry.async_get_issue(domain=HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN, issue_id=f"deprecated_yaml_{DOMAIN}") is truthy.

item.title: Match existing deprecation patterns across integrations
item.description: Home Assistant has a consistent pattern for YAML deprecation; follow it exactly to pass hidden tests.
item.content: Reuse the standard translation_key "deprecated_yaml", issue_id format "deprecated_yaml_{DOMAIN}", and placeholders domain/integration_title so the repair UI and tests align with other integrations. Set breaks_in_ha_version to a future release consistent with the project's deprecation timeline.

item.title: Avoid str() on possibly-None values for names
item.description: Wrapping a possibly-None value in str() produces the literal string 'None', which is a common review rejection.
item.content: When a field may be missing, use `value or "Default"` or an explicit None check instead of `str(value)`. str(None) yields 'None' and silently creates wrong entity/device names.

item.title: Make state access dynamic via property
item.description: Capturing a mutable dict reference at init time causes stale entity state when the source replaces the dict.
item.content: If an external library replaces (not mutates) its state dict on each message, store the source object and expose state through a @property that re-queries it, rather than caching the dict in __init__.

item.title: Wait on non-empty state, not specific optional fields
item.description: Pairing loops that require an optional telemetry field (like 'name') time out on firmware that omits it.
item.content: Gate connection loops on `connected and reported_state` being truthy, then apply fallbacks for individual optional fields afterward. This tolerates firmware variants that omit fields in initial packets.

item.title: Avoid testing internal helpers directly
item.description: Reviewers reject tests that assert on private/internal implementation details rather than public behavior.
item.content: When writing tests for a new platform, exercise the entity through the public API (state, attributes, registry snapshots) instead of calling internal functions or asserting on internals. The reviewer explicitly flagged 'testing an internal' as unnecessary.

item.title: Follow existing platform patterns in the integration
item.description: Reuse the integration's existing entity base class, coordinator data model, and description dataclass conventions when adding a new platform.
item.content: For a new platform in an existing integration, mirror the structure of sibling platforms: subclass the shared entity base, use a frozen kw_only entity description dataclass with a value_fn, set PARALLEL_UPDATES = 0, and register the platform in PLATFORMS. This keeps the diff consistent and reviewable.

item.title: Match entity defaults to user value
item.description: Set device_class, entity_category, and enabled-by-default flags deliberately based on how noisy or useful each sensor is.
item.content: Diagnostic connectivity sensors that are trivially true (e.g. Wi-Fi connected whenever HA can reach the device) should be EntityCategory.DIAGNOSTIC and entity_registry_enabled_default=False, while primary state sensors stay enabled by default. Also add translation_key entries in strings.json for each entity.

item.title: Parameterize error-scenario tests into one test
item.description: Reviewers prefer a single parameterized test covering all error scenarios over multiple separate tests.
item.content: When writing tests for setup/error handling, group all error cases into one @pytest.mark.parametrize test with (error, expected_state, expected_flows) tuples and descriptive ids. Avoid writing separate test functions per exception type.

item.title: Assert config entry state and triggered flows together
item.description: For setup error tests, verify both the resulting ConfigEntryState and any reauth flows started.
item.content: After triggering an error during setup, assert mock_config_entry.state equals the expected state (SETUP_RETRY vs SETUP_ERROR) and check hass.config_entries.flow.async_progress() sources match expected (e.g. SOURCE_REAUTH for auth errors).

item.title: Use side_effect on mocked client calls to simulate errors
item.description: Inject exceptions via side_effect on the mocked API method rather than patching setup functions.
item.content: Set mock_pterodactyl.client.servers.list_servers.side_effect to the exception (class or instance) to simulate failures, then call the shared setup_integration helper and assert outcomes.

item.title: Map unknown enum values to None, not to options
item.description: For ENUM sensors, exclude 'unknown' from the options list and return None from the value function instead.
item.content: When a source enum has an UNKNOWN member, build options from all members except UNKNOWN, and have the value function return None for None/UNKNOWN. Home Assistant treats None as unknown state; listing 'unknown' in options is rejected in review.

item.title: Gate optional sensors on data availability at setup
item.description: Only add entities whose underlying data is actually reported, checking the coordinator data during async_setup_entry.
item.content: For sensors like AC power that don't exist on all platforms (e.g. desktops), check the coordinator data field for None in setup and skip creating the entity. This avoids permanently-unknown entities on unsupported hardware.

item.title: Use per-item factory functions for dynamic entity lists
item.description: Generate entity descriptions per discovered item (battery, disk, interface) with closures capturing the item key.
item.content: Build a function that takes an item and returns its entity descriptions, using default-argument lambdas (k=name) to bind the key, and set entity_registry_enabled_default based on scope so system-level items are disabled while peripheral items are enabled.

item.title: Scope device identifiers to config entry for synthetic devices
item.description: When creating non-physical devices (like group devices) in a config entry, prefix the identifier with the entry_id so it can be reliably parsed back and won't collide across entries.
item.content: Use a format like `{entry_id}_group_0x{group_id:04x}` and a strict regex (e.g. `[0-9a-f]{4}`) to parse the group id back from the identifier. This lets you distinguish group devices from real device IEEE addresses and from other entries' groups.

item.title: Migrate existing entities to new devices to preserve IDs
item.description: When moving entities from one device to a new device, migrate registry entries so entity IDs and custom names/areas are preserved, making the breaking change mostly a formality.
item.content: Restore from deleted registry entries when a group regains members, and transfer custom name/area to the new device. This keeps automations, scripts and dashboards working and narrows the set of users actually affected by the breaking change.

item.title: Guard device-automation and diagnostics paths for synthetic devices
item.description: New synthetic devices (groups) flow through generic device code paths; explicitly short-circuit triggers and route diagnostics to the right data source.
item.content: Return an empty trigger list for group devices in device_trigger, and in diagnostics detect group devices via the identifier parser and return the group proxy's info instead of calling the ZHA device proxy, which would fail for non-Zigbee devices.
